questions.text: In first-angle projection, where is the top view conventionally placed relative to the front view?
options: Above
Below
Always overlaid
Only to the right

questions.text: Which line convention represents an edge hidden from the current view?
options: Thin dashed line
Continuous thick line
Dimension line
Centre line only

questions.text: What does a scale of 1:2 mean?
options: Drawing is twice actual size
Drawing equals actual size
Drawing is half actual size
Scale is unrelated to actual size

questions.text: A line is inclined to both principal projection planes. Why are both orthographic projections shorter than its true length?
options: The scale is always wrong
Both projections must be redrawn as circles
The object is not three-dimensional
A line not parallel to a projection plane is foreshortened in that view

questions.text: An inclined plane's true shape is not visible in the principal views. Which method is suitable?
options: Use an auxiliary plane parallel to the inclined surface
Enlarge the front view only
Replace dimensions with an isometric sketch
Use a centre line as its boundary

questions.text: Why can a circle appear elliptical in an isometric view?
options: The original circle must be inaccurate
Its plane is projected obliquely in the isometric representation
Every circle is required to become a rectangle
The scale has necessarily been applied incorrectly

questions.text: An object contains an internal bore that is obscured by many hidden edges. Which drawing approach best communicates the internal feature and preserves useful external information?
options: Delete all dimensions
Show only hidden lines and omit the outside shape
Use a suitable sectional view with necessary external geometry and dimensions
Replace the bore boundary with a centre line

questions.text: A line is parallel to VP but inclined to HP. Which statement is correct?
options: Both projections always show true length
The top view shows true length in every case
Neither view can show true length
The front view shows true length; the top view is foreshortened

questions.text: Which check best verifies plotted points for an ellipse defined by two foci?
options: The sum of distances from each point to both foci remains constant
Each point has equal distance to one focus only
All points lie on the same circle centred at one focus
Every tangent passes through both foci

questions.text: Front, top and side views conflict with an isometric sketch. What should be checked first?
options: Change the isometric scale until it looks right
Compare dimensions and feature locations across views and confirm first-/third-angle convention
Delete hidden lines and dimensions
Assume the pictorial view overrides all dimensions
